name: Kansas
source: Kansas Department of Revenue 2025 income tax booklet (https://ksrevenue.gov/incomebook25.html, read 2026-10-22): tax computation 5.2% to 23,000 (46,000 joint) and 5.58% above, standard deduction 3,605 / 8,240 with the 65-or-older amounts, exemption allowance 9,160 / 18,320 and 2,320 per dependent, Social Security subtracted, only public pensions (KPERS, federal, military) exempt; second source Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/state-income-tax-rates-2026/) (same figures for 2026)

state_base.note: Kansas starts from federal AGI, so 401(k) deferrals and HSA deposits stay deductible as on the federal return (confirmed primary: https://ksrevenue.gov/incomebook25.html, validation run 3, 2026-10-22).

standard_deduction.note: Standard deduction 3,605 single, 8,240 joint and 4,120 married filing separately (2025 booklet, https://ksrevenue.gov/incomebook25.html, confirmed primary, validation run 2, 2026-10-22); separate returns use the single brackets in a table of their own so the deduction can differ.

exemptions.note: Exemption allowance 9,160 single, 18,320 joint, 2,320 per dependent. senior is the additional standard deduction at 65: 850 single (4,455 less 3,605) and 700 per person joint (8,940 less 8,240); the model uses 850 for both. A separate return takes the single exemption allowance (9,160).

estate_inheritance.note: Kansas has no estate tax (repealed for deaths from 2010) and no inheritance tax (state-costs.csv: none; AARP 2026 list of estate and inheritance tax states does not include Kansas). Confirmed primary on https://ksrevenue.gov/taxnotices/notice10-07.pdf (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

social_security.note: From tax year 2024 Kansas subtracts all Social Security benefits included in federal AGI (2025 booklet, Schedule S line A10; state-costs.csv ss_taxed 'N (2024+)').

local_income_tax.check_at: Kansas city and county tax codes
local_income_tax.note: Kansas cities and counties levy no income tax on residents (state-costs.csv local_income_tax none).

sales_tax.check_at: Kansas revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://www.salestaxinstitute.com/resources/kansas-reduces-sales-and-use-tax-rate-on-food-and-food-ingredients and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: 0.0871 from the state's own source (Kansas: the dealer collects the state 6.5% plus the local rate, so the combined rate (https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pub1526.html, validation run 3)). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: yes); research note: State food rate 0% from 2025-01-01; city and county taxes still apply; food sales tax refund credit status not checked. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.check_at: Kansas Department of Revenue vehicle property tax lookup (https://mvs.dmv.kdor.ks.gov/VehiclePropertyTaxLookup) and county mill levies
car_taxes.source: Estimate from the Kansas method (county mill levy times the taxable value of the vehicle class, 15% depreciation a year; 12 minimum for cars 15 years or older) and a registration fee of about 40; no published average found
car_taxes.note: Kansas: an annual county property tax on vehicles plus registration. For a car bought new at about 40,000 the tax falls from roughly 900 in the first year as the value depreciates; about 450 a year averaged over ten years with registration (rough estimate, no published average). Typical car, averaged over about ten years of ownership; registration and vehicle taxes only (no title, plate or inspection fees). Set by hand after the import: rerunning importStateCosts.py resets it to 0.

fuel.source: Excise: https://klrd.gov/state-motor-fuels-taxes-and-fuel-use/ (validation run 2, 2026-10-22); price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel: 0.24 (24 cents/gal gasoline, unchanged since 2003); average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Kansas insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
